factual_claims.source_evidence: Board of Directors' Report (page 39) and Note 69 (page 70) confirm EBIT of SEK 73,478 thousand (2025) vs. 60,677 thousand (2024, +21.1%), with operating margin rising to 31% from 28%.

factual_claims.claim: Lower financing costs contributed to the improvement: interest expenses and similar charges declined to SEK 82.0 million from SEK 88.7 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Board of Directors' Report (page 39) states interest expenses and similar charges were SEK 82.0 million (2025) vs. 88.7 million (2024). Note 16 (page 64) details refinancing reducing interest costs.

factual_claims.claim: Nevertheless, the Group reported a loss after tax of SEK 7.2 million, compared with a loss of SEK 32.9 million in 2024.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Board of Directors' Report (page 39) and Income Statement (page 42) show profit after tax of SEK -7,206 thousand (2025) vs. -32,944 thousand (2024).

factual_claims.claim: The result included a negative currency effect of SEK 3.8 million and a one-off cost of SEK 3.5 million; the CEO stated that profit adjusted for these items was SEK 0.1 million, compared with negative SEK 34.7 million in 2024.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Board of Directors' Report (page 39) notes exchange rate difference of SEK -3.8 million. CEO commentary (page 5) states adjusted profit was SEK 0.1 million (vs. -34.7 million in 2024).

factual_claims.claim: Operationally, produced electricity increased 30% to 327.8 million kWh, and installed capacity grew 16% to 395.8 MW from 340.1 MW through the addition of 55.7 MW.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Board of Directors' Report (page 39) and Operations section (page 16) confirm produced electricity of 327.8 million kWh (2025) vs. 252.6 million kWh (2024, +30%), installed capacity of 395.8 MW (2025) vs. 340.1 MW (2024), with 55.7 MW added.

factual_claims.claim: The portfolio comprised 216 installations at year-end.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Operations section (page 16) states: 'As of December 31, 2025, Gigasun had a portfolio of 216 electricity-generating solar energy installations.'

factual_claims.claim: The company signed 17 contracts representing approximately 41.8 MW of capacity, although signed orders at year-end were reported at 16.4 MW.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Board of Directors' Report (page 39) states: 'The company signed 17 (15) contracts representing total installed capacity of 41.7 (56.6) MW. At the end of the year, the company had 16.4 (38.8) MW in signed orders.'

factual_claims.claim: Electricity tariffs in Jiangsu and Anhui reduced realized prices per kWh by approximately 8% in the second half, with an estimated 3–4% impact on revenue from the existing portfolio.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: CEO commentary (page 5) states: 'During mid-2025, electricity tariffs in the Jiangsu and Anhui provinces were adjusted... reduced the realized price per kWh by approximately 8 percent... impact on our existing project portfolio is manageable and amounts to approximately a 3–4 percent reduction in revenue.'

factual_claims.claim: Gigasun stated that lower financing and construction costs were expected to offset this pressure.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: CEO commentary (page 5) states: 'Lower financing costs, combined with declining construction costs for new projects and upgrades, are expected to contribute to gradually improved earnings going forward.'

factual_claims.claim: Financing remained a central issue.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Risk factors (page 29) and refinancing details (pages 39, 64-67) emphasize financing as a critical challenge, with explicit statements about refinancing needs and debt management.

factual_claims.claim: Refinancing agreements totaling approximately SEK 1.242 billion at 3.60% over ten years were initiated, while the SOLT4 bond was extended to 8 November 2026.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Board of Directors' Report (page 39) and Note 16 (page 64) detail refinancing of SEK 1,242 million (CNY 880 million) at 3.60% over 10 years, and extension of SOLT4 bond to November 8, 2026.

factual_claims.claim: Interest-bearing debt declined to SEK 1.383 billion from SEK 1.483 billion, but cash fell to SEK 45.1 million from SEK 89.9 million and the equity ratio decreased to 21% from 23%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Balance Sheet (page 43) shows interest-bearing debt of SEK 1,382,613 thousand (2025) vs. 1,483,061 thousand (2024). Cash and bank balances were SEK 45,149 thousand (2025) vs. 89,889 thousand (2024). Equity ratio was 21% (2025) vs. 23% (2024).

factual_claims.claim: The Group’s cash flow was negative SEK 34.9 million, as operating cash flow of SEK 101.1 million did not cover investments of SEK 208.1 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Cash Flow Statement (page 46) shows cash flow from operating activities of SEK 101,058 thousand, investing activities of SEK -208,101 thousand, resulting in a net cash flow of SEK -34,902 thousand.

factual_claims.claim: Management stated that failure to secure further financing in 2026 would create significant uncertainty regarding the Group’s ability to continue under its current business plan.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: Going Concern assessment (page 53) states: 'If the company is not successful with new financing, the company believes that there is significant uncertainty regarding going concern in the current business plan.'
